figures.label: Formal Training Path Start Mbbs
figures.source: A radiologist is a full medical doctor, MBBS, then an MD or DNB in Radiodiagnosis through NEET-PG, one of the most competitive postgraduate medical specialisations to get a seat in. This is a 9-11 year formal training path from the start of MBBS.
figures.text: A radiologist is a full medical doctor, MBBS, then an MD or DNB in Radiodiagnosis through NEET-PG, one of the most competitive postgraduate medical specialisations to get a seat in. This is a 9-11 year formal training path from the start of MBBS.

figures.label: Pay Range
figures.source: A radiology or imaging technician (often called a radiographer) operates the imaging equipment, X-ray, CT, MRI, ultrasound machines, under a radiologist's supervision. This is a 2-4 year BSc or diploma route, not a medical degree, and does not qualify someone to interpret scans or diagnose.
